stories.title: Israel president urges compromise after divisive election
summary: The election saw soaring support for lists from the Arab minority, descendants of Palestinians who stayed in Israel after its 1948 creation and who have often been outraged by the harsh rhetoric and actions of Netanyahu’s hard-right government.

Buoyed by US elections Eisenkot has warned Netanyahu against launching a new war with his ally Trump against Iran, which could help the Israeli prime minister push for a unity government or to run out the clock until new elections.
Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister who has been in power on and off for nearly two decades, has called for a “broad national government” — with himself at the top.

stories.title: 'United opposition' gathers at Fazl's Islamabad residence, vows stronger alliance
summary: After a meeting during which they discussed several matters, including the emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, JUI-F and TTAP decided to form committees to resolve mutual differences and take forward consultations on a multi-party conference (MPC).
On Aug 20, following a meeting between Fazl and Achakzai, the alliance and JUI-F had announced plans to form a “united opposition”.

In the days preceding the emergency, political tensions between the Centre and the opposition — including the PTI, which was in power in KP — had remained high since Imran’s party announced a protest march to Islamabad to demand his release.

stories.title: Seeing red in Iran
summary: One of the CIA’s first interventions, against Iranian democracy in the early 1950s, was justified as a blow against communist influence, even though the popular nationalist Mohammad Mossadegh was barely left of centre.

Iran had only recently released the hostages taken at the US embassy, but while the American cold warriors might not have been fans of the clergy, in their blinkered worldview the communist threat was paramount.

The suspicion was that Moscow’s arms and gold were preparing Tudeh for a coup that could pave the way for a Soviet invasion, as in Afghanistan, and further tilt the Cold War imbalance towards communism.

stories.title: Big money flops as Democrats sweep US Congress
summary: Democrat James Talarico defeated Paxton, a close Trump ally, to become the first Democrat to win statewide office in Texas since 1994. “In this race, we went up against our own Goliaths.
In Ohio, Democrat Sherrod Brown unseated Republican Senator Jon Husted in the country’s second most expensive race, with more than $500m spent.
In Ohio, biotech billionaire Vivek Ramaswamy lost the governor’s race to Democrat Amy Acton after putting an estimated $36m of his own money into it.

Previously, on July 17, the petroleum minister announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

stories.title: 38 briefly detained in Karachi as police baton-charge protesters headed towards CM House
summary: KARACHI: Thirty-eight people were released after brief detention on Wednesday as police used tear gas and batons against protesting teachers headed towards Chief Minister House from Karachi Press Club (KPC).
Speaking to Dawn earlier in the day, the DIG noted that a teachers’ organisation had announced a protest at the KPC, with a march planned toward the CM House.
According to Nizamani, as the protesters moved from KPC towards CM House, police resorted to tear gas and a baton charge.

stories.title: Govt says Islamabad's One Constitution Avenue to be turned into a five-star hotel
summary: The federal government on Wednesday said that a joint investigation team had revealed that Islamabad’s One Constitution Avenue was built on “irregularities and rigging” and announced that the residential building will soon be turned into a five-star hotel.
The building was initially supposed to be a five-star hotel project; however, instead of functioning as a five-star hotel, it was converted into residential apartments and commercial areas.

Addressing a press conference on Wednesday alongside Information Minister Attaullah Tarar and State Minister for Interior Tallal Chaudhry, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal said the JIT presented its report to the federal cabinet today, noting that the project was fraudulent.

stories.title: Asif says Chaudhry Salik's remarks about corruption in Punjab 'beyond my understanding'
summary: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif said on Wednesday that Minister for Overseas Pakistanis Chaudhry Salik Hussain’s remarks regarding corruption in Punjab were “beyond my understanding”.

In a post on the social media platform X on Wednesday, Asif said, “Chaudhry Salik Sahib is very respected in my eyes; I respect his elders just as I respect my own. “His statement regarding corruption in Punjab is beyond my limited political understanding.
The minister’s remarks had also drawn a sharp rebuttal from Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari, who advised Salik not to “bite the hand that feeds him”.

stories.title: AI, Gulf policy shifts threaten migrant jobs
summary: Francoise De Bel-Air, Senior Fellow at the Gulf Labour Markets, Migration and Population (GLMM) programme, said opportunities were growing for skilled professionals across North America, Europe and the Gulf.

The speakers were of the view that Pakistan's migration showed both continuity and change, with traditional labour migration to the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states continuing alongside growing skilled migration to Western countries.
They added that migration pressures in countries such as Pakistan and Nepal were likely to stay high because of demographic shifts and limited domestic opportunities.

stories.title: Super tax to be abolished: FBR chief
summary: To make the track and trace system operational, the FBR will work with the pharmaceutical industry to implement a model similar to that of the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan (DRAP).
He said the FBR's objective was to improve the tax system and facilitate the business community.
He urged industrialists and traders to cooperate with the FBR in identifying and eliminating elements involved in tax evasion so that the tax system could be made more transparent and effective.

stories.title: EDF decides to invest in govt securities
summary: The government has allowed the Export Development Fund (EDF) board, which works under the Ministry of Commerce, to invest in government securities.

The Ministry of Commerce had asked the Economic Coordination Committee (ECC) of the cabinet to permit the EDF board to transfer funds from the public/treasury account to its commercial bank account for onward investment in government papers.

The fund is managed by the EDF board under the Ministry of Commerce.Following legislative amendments to the EDF Act, 1999 and with the president's approval on January 26, 2026, the federal government had appointed new members of the EDF board.

stories.title: Rizwan stages resounding comeback in domestic cricket after England tour controversy
summary: The former Test regular had endured a lean run with the bat in England, scoring just 61 runs in four innings before the squad overhaul and subsequent investigation into alleged dressing-room issues and related matters.

Lean outing for Babar Elsewhere, Babar Azam endured another modest outing, scoring just 28 as Lahore Whites were bowled out for 234 in 49.2 overs against Fata at the Diamond Cricket Ground in Islamabad, conceding a first-innings lead of 128 runs.
At the National Ground in Islamabad, Karachi Blues scored 280 to secure a slender first-innings lead of 39 runs over Sialkot Blues, who closed the day at 13 without loss.

stories.title: Democrats win US Congress in midterm rout of Trump
summary: Democrat James Talarico ousted a Trump-backed Senate candidate, while Gina Hinojosa unseated Republican governor Greg Abbott, ending decades of Republican control of the state’s top office.
In California, Democrat Xavier Becerra handily defeated Donald Trump-backed Republican Steve Hilton in the race to become the governor, US networks said.

Democrats held onto three House districts in Florida that Republican lawmakers had redrawn earlier this year, all of which backed Trump by at least nine percentage points, according to media projections.

stories.title: PIA to run 3 weekly direct flights between Islamabad and Birmingham from Dec 1
summary: Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) announced on Wednesday that it is launching three weekly direct flights between Islamabad and Birmingham from Dec 1.

The statement added that the UK was a “highly important” air route for the airline, noting that efforts were being made to increase the total number of weekly flights between the country and Pakistan to 23.
In July 2025, the UK also removed Pakistan from its Air Safety List, allowing Pakistani airlines to apply to operate flights in Britain.

stories.title: ECP objects to retired SC judge's remarks about 2023 ruling on polls in Punjab and KP, reserved seats case
summary: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Wednesday objected to remarks made by former senior puisne judge of the Supreme Court of Pakistan, Mansoor Ali Shah, regarding polls in KP and Punjab and the reserved seats case pertaining to the PTI.
The electoral watchdog said that Shah had claimed that the SC’s majority decision about the elections in 2023 was a 4-3 verdict and that the suo motu notice and relevant petitions were dismissed.
The ECP further stated that PTI held intra-party elections after five years and its proceedings remained pending before the commission as the “PTI itself has taken a stay order from a high court”.

stories.title: PTI seeks Imran's immediate transfer to Shifa International Hospital over renewed blood pressure concerns
summary: In the meeting's aftermath, Imran's sister Rubina Khan said her brother had conveyed through his lawyer that his blood pressure had shot up to 192.
Sharing his aunt's statement on X, Imran's son Kasim said: “This high blood pressure is not normal.

He accused the government of endangering the life and fundamental rights of the country's most popular political leader by denying him adequate medical facilities, access to his family and treatment of his choice.

stories.title: 'We did it!': Democrat El-Sayed hails US Senate win, becomes first Muslim elected to upper chamber of Congress
summary: During the race, El-Sayed drew huge campaign crowds across the state, even in deeply conservative Republican areas.
The victory made El-Sayed the first Democratic doctor in the Senate since 1969. “Everybody in politics is so trash.
Addressing the vice president, El-Sayed said in his victory speech, “you’re constitutionally obligated to swear me in in January”.

stories.title: Opp forms APC committees, vows countrywide movement against govt after huddle
summary: The JUI-F chief said the opposition was raising national issues through political discourse, but the government was targeting individuals instead of addressing the concerns.

Opposition huddle at Fazl's residence Earlier, opposition parties gathered at Fazl's residence to discuss the prevailing political situation, including the imposition of governor's rule and an emergency in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P).
Following the imposition of the emergency and governor's rule, Fazl accused the government of backing out of negotiations with the PTI and the opposition despite initially agreeing to their demands.

stories.title: Iran supreme leader says those expecting US policy shift 'seriously mistaken'
summary: Democrats seized control of the US Congress in Tuesday’s midterms, reflecting anger over living costs, tariffs and the US war against Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring.

US and Israeli leaders have in recent days threatened to resume attacks against Iran. “Should such aggressions be repeated, the war’s scope will become much wider,” said Khamenei, who has yet to appear in public since he took power in March.

Iran’s judiciary chief Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei also hailed the election results, saying Trump had been “defeated both militarily and politically”. “We will certainly inflict further defeats on him,” he added.

stories.title: US Vice President Vance says Iran war is ‘the reason we lost’ midterms
summary: US Vice President JD Vance said on Wednesday that the Iran war had doomed Republicans in the midterm elections, moving to distance himself from the unpopular conflict ahead of a possible 2028 White House run. “The reason we lost is the war.

Vance also acknowledged that Republican voters who backed Trump and himself two years ago had switched sides due to the war and its effects on the US economy. “The main problem is that many people who voted for Trump/Vance in 2024 voted for Democrats in 2026,” Vance said.

"The American people don't know what the heck we're fighting for in Iran." Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer calls for an end to the war, accusing President Trump of repeatedly shifting his explanation for the U.S. mission.

stories.title: 'Clear message' by Americans: US politicians react to Democratic win in US midterms
summary: President Trump, meanwhile, in comments to Fox News, said, “Congratulations to the Democrats — they did a good job.

Florida Governor Ron DeSantis pointed out that it was “unlikely” Republicans would recapture Congress in 2028, looking at the Senate map and given the “massive” margin in the House. “Might not have a shot at Senate control until 2032,” he added.
CNN cited DeSantis as saying that Republicans underemphasised the impact of high gas prices due to the Iran war, although he did not name Trump specifically. “Listen, we’ve just got to be honest.

stories.title: Federal cabinet ratifies defence agreement with Kuwait
summary: The federal cabinet on Wednesday ratified the defence cooperation agreement between Pakistan and Kuwait, according to a handout by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO). “The federal cabinet ratified a defence cooperation agreement between Pakistan and Kuwait.
The statement also said that the cabinet approved the transfer of powers delegated to the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister to the province’s governor.

Last month, Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir, accompanied by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, visited Iran as part of Pakistan’s efforts to mediate between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Govt slashes petrol by Rs7.06, diesel by Rs3.71 for Nov 5
summary: The federal government on Wednesday slashed the price of petrol by Rs7.06 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.71 per litre for November 5.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs362 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs387.81 per litre for Thursday.
The latest revision comes a day after the government reduced the price of petrol by Rs5.45 per litre and that of HSD by Rs3.68 for November 4.

stories.title: Trump hand-picked Senate candidates. Republicans paid the price
summary: US President Donald Trump asked voters to pretend he was on the ballot in the midterm elections and handpicked Republican candidates in some of the country’s most consequential Senate races.
Trump-backed candidates in South Carolina, North Carolina and Texas all lost, while the president’s preferred pick trailed in early results in Michigan.

In Texas, Trump intervened in a messy Republican primary election to promote scandal-plagued Attorney General Ken Paxton over Senator John Cornyn, a Trump ally who some in the party considered a safer pick in the general election.

stories.title: Pakistan, UK express concern at threat posed by terrorist groups operating in and from Afghanistan: FO
summary: Pakistan and the United Kingdom on Wednesday expressed concerns over the ongoing threat from terrorist groups operating in and from Afghanistan, the Foreign Office said.

The UK delegation also expressed condolences over the loss of innocent lives in terrorist attacks in Pakistan and reiterated that it stood with the country in the fight against terrorism, the statement added.
Pakistan and the European Union (EU) have also agreed to strengthen cooperation at multilateral forums, including the United Nations.

stories.title: Explainer: What does Democratic control of Congress mean for Trump?
summary: Democrats’ victory in the US midterm elections has handed them control of both chambers of Congress, setting up a period of divided government that could complicate President Donald Trump’s agenda during the final two years of his term.

When the new Congress convenes in January 2027, Trump will face a Democratic-controlled House of Representatives and Senate, limiting his ability to advance legislation and potentially complicating his administration’s spending priorities.
Impeachment issue Democrats could technically launch another impeachment process against Trump, as the House has the power to impeach a president with a simple majority.

stories.title: Israeli president receives official election results as committee rejects fraud allegations
summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog on Wednesday received the official results of last week's parliamentary elections as the Central Elections Committee rejected fraud allegations raised by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and right-wing parties.
Earlier Wednesday, the committee approved the final results, with 15 members voting in favor, two against and 14 abstaining, according to Ynet.

Also Read: Eisenkot says Netanyahu's bid to discredit Israeli election results has 'failed' Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot is expected to receive 48 recommendations from Yashar, Yachad, the Democrats and Yisrael Beytenu.

stories.title: Troops deployed in Indonesia as president sacks aide accused of wiretapping
summary: Indonesia's president sacked his chief of staff on Wednesday after his arrest in a wiretapping scandal ‌that the government said pointed to treason, as the military said thousands of troops were being mobilised in the capital to boost security.

Military mobilized to ‘safeguard and protect stability' Troops were deployed to Jakarta to "safeguard and ​protect the stability of Indonesia's security," navy spokesperson Tunggul said late on Wednesday.

Sana Jaffrey, a state-building ⁠researcher at ​the Australian National University, said the troop deployment in Jakarta could signal concerns about tension ​between the military and police loyal to former chief Listyo.

stories.title: Schools in Sindh to remain closed on Nov 9 on account of Iqbal Day
summary: The Sindh government announced on Wednesday that all public and private schools across the province would remain closed on Nov 9 (Monday) to mark the birth anniversary of Dr Allama Muhammad Iqbal, the national poet of Pakistan.
Born on November 9, 1877, in Sialkot, Iqbal was a distinguished poet, a scholar, a gifted philosopher and Pakistan’s ideological founder.

Iqbal Day was on the calendar of national public holidays for decades, but the interior ministry, through a circular issued on November 4, 2015, announced the cancellation of the day as an annual holiday without specifying a reason.

stories.title: Iranian officials gloat as US voters deal blow to Trump
summary: Iran's government savoured the stinging rebuke delivered to Donald Trump in the midterm elections, declaring voters had rejected the war launched by ​the US president even as Tehran remained on high alert for the possibility of renewed strikes.

Mediators have intensified efforts to end the war amid fears it ​could reignite after the election, with Trump on Tuesday declining to rule out a resumption of combat operations after the vote and Iran planning wider retaliation if war resumes.

'Iran’s shadow over US elections' Ahead of the US election, senior Iranian officials told Reuters that Tehran was deliberately prolonging talks with ​the US to weaken Trump politically ahead of the ​vote.

stories.title: ICJ to rule on Myanmar genocide case over Rohingya on Nov 19
summary: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) would deliver its judgment on November 19 on whether Myanmar violated the UN Genocide Convention in its treatment of the Rohingya Muslim minority, the court announced on Tuesday.
The lawsuit accuses Myanmar of violating its obligations under the 1948 Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide during military operations against the Rohingya.
The Rohingya are a stateless Muslim minority who have faced decades of discrimination and displacement in Myanmar.

stories.title: IHC fixes Imran and Bushra's appeals against sentences in £190m case for Nov 10
summary: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Wednesday fixed the hearing of the appeals of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan and his wife Bushra Bibi against their convictions in the £190 million case for November 10.

Read: IHC gives Imran final opportunity to argue £190m case appeals At the previous hearing, the court had adjourned the proceedings without taking up the matter following a request by Imran’s counsel, Barrister Salman Safdar.
In January 2025, an Islamabad accountability court sentenced Imran to 14 years and Bushra to seven years in prison in the reference filed by the National Accountability Bureau.

stories.title: PIA to launch three direct weekly Islamabad-Birmingham flights from Dec 1
summary: Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) on Wednesday said it would launch three weekly direct flights between Islamabad and Birmingham from December 1, expanding its UK network to facilitate Pakistani residents in northern and central parts of Britain.
Read: PIA resumes UK flights after five-year ban On September 3, PIA decided to expand its air operations to London, increasing the number of weekly flights to seven from October 27.
PIA resumed direct flights to Britain in October last year, months after UK authorities ended a five-year suspension imposed over aviation safety concerns.

stories.title: UK ban on Palestine Action is challenged at top court, some protesters arrested
summary: A co-founder of Palestine Action challenged Britain's decision to ban ​the campaign group as a terrorist organisation at the UK Supreme Court on Wednesday, arguing that ‌the move was disproportionate and undermined counter-terrorism laws.

There have been more than 3,600 arrests linked to support for Palestine Action between proscription ​in July 2025 and this June, representing more than one-third of all terrorism arrests in Britain since 9/11, according to Home Office statistics.

Lawyers representing Huda Ammori, who co-founded Palestine Action, said that, at the time ​the group was proscribed, government ​officials had assessed that ⁠just three of 385 actions carried out over five years had met the definition of terrorism.

stories.title: Sonam Kapoor revisits Elizabeth Taylor’s iconic Bulgari emerald necklace after Kim Kardashian moment
summary: After Kim Kardashian recently brought Elizabeth Taylor's iconic emerald-and-diamond Bulgari necklace back into the spotlight, the Bollywood actor shared throwback photographs of herself wearing the legendary piece.
The necklace was created by Italian luxury jewellery house Bulgari around 1962, when Taylor was in Rome filming Cleopatra.
Burton, who famously indulged Taylor's love of extravagant jewellery, gifted her an extraordinary collection of Bulgari emerald pieces over the course of their relationship.

stories.title: 'It is a cappuccino. It can't be $10,' says Harry Styles about NYC coffee prices
summary: Singer Harry Styles, who recently completed a 30-show residency at Madison Square Garden in New York, ​thought prices for coffee in the city were some ‌of the spookiest things he saw around Halloween.
Some fans, in comments after ​the video, thought it was amusing that such a wealthy and successful personality would complain about such an ordinary thing as the price for a ​cup of coffee.
Coffee companies say ⁠they ​had to cut profit margins during the ​cost shock to prevent prices rising even more, and are now in a period ​of recovering their margins.

stories.title: SSGC announces winter gas supply schedule for Sindh, Balochistan
summary: KARACHI: The Sui Southern Gas Company (SSGC) on Wednesday announced the gas supply schedule for the winter season, under which three slots have been fixed for supply to domestic consumers, in line with federal government directives.

Gas availability under new schedule: 6:30am-9am (Breakfast) 12pm-2:30pm (Lunch) 6pm-9pm (Dinner) The SSGC shared the schedule on its website and social media platforms, saying that it was “prioritising domestic consumers by ensuring supply during meal times”.
For the past some years, SSGC’s consumers have not been getting round-the-clock gas supply.

stories.title: Naqvi says One Constitution Avenue to be converted into five-star hotel in 'coming months'
summary: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi announced on Wednesday that One Constitution Avenue would be converted into a five-star hotel, assuring that all those entitled to compensation would be paid their dues.

He said: "The prime minister had ordered an inquiry committee into the fraud that took place in the name of One Constitution Avenue, and today the JIT report was placed before the cabinet, which consisted of members from NAB, FIA, FBR, SECP, IB and ISI.
On May 4, the IHC issued a detailed verdict on the One Constitution Avenue project, upholding the Capital Development Authority's (CDA) decision and ruling that the buyers lack ownership rights.

stories.title: Israel election commission rejects Netanyahu charges of fraud
summary: Israeli electoral authorities on Wednesday rejected allegations promoted by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of fraud by Arab parties, who could hold the key to removing him from power after a divisive vote.

President Isaac Herzog will at noon (1000 GMT) officially receive the results of the October 27 election as he decides whether to give Netanyahu or his rival Gadi Eisenkot the first chance to form a government, with neither commanding enough votes alone.

He had earlier warned Netanyahu against launching a new war with his close ally US President Donald Trump against Iran, which could help the Israeli prime minister push for a unity government or to run out the clock until new elections.

stories.title: Mariyam Nafees hits back at intrusive questions about having another child
summary: Actor Mariyam Nafees has hit back at people who repeatedly question her about having another child, expressing frustration over the intrusion into her personal life during a recent Instagram Q&A session.

The actor addressed the matter after a follower asked her, “Next baby when?”, prompting a sarcastic response about people's tendency to interfere in celebrities' family planning. “Life would be going so well and then people would pop up with their questions,” she said.

While the actor has remained candid about different aspects of motherhood, her latest response makes one thing clear: being a public figure does not mean celebrities are obliged to answer every personal question about their marriages, children or plans to expand their families.
